items.description:
The registry generator rendered the audit trail only into Markdown. render_item emitted the item_history block, the Reopened-Details line and the Operator-Block-Details line, while html_documents enumerated six item fields and pdf_documents seven, in both cases with no history and no lifecycle detail. The consequence surfaced as a failed qualification gate rather than as a review finding: closing HRD-024 with a reason that named HRD-034 put that identifier into Fixed.md, and scripts/verify_workable_items.py check pdf-documents-current, which extracts HRD identifiers from each PDF with pdftotext and requires the set its Markdown sibling carries, reported Fixed.pdf as stale even though export had written it one second earlier. The PDF was current and simply did not render the text, so the gate was describing a generator defect as a currency defect. Fixed by giving all three long-form renderers one source of truth: long_form_fields(item, db) returns every label and value an item carries, including conditional reopen and operator-block details, and history_lines(db, atm_id) formats the audit trail once for Markdown, HTML and PDF.

Severity: High
Registry status: Fixed (→ Fixed.md)
Reopens: 0
Affected scope: scripts/workable_items.py render_item, html_documents and pdf_documents; scripts/verify_workable_items.py mutation cases; tests/test_workable_items.py; every derived document under docs/.
Reproduction: Close any item with a reason naming a different HRD identifier, run export with PDF enabled, then compare identifier sets: pdftotext docs/Fixed.pdf carries fewer HRD identifiers than docs/Fixed.md, and verify_workable_items.py reports pdf-documents-current FAIL with the missing identifier attributed to the Markdown side.
Acceptance: Markdown, HTML and PDF long-form documents each render every field long_form_fields returns plus the full item history; tests.test_workable_items.test_derived_documents_carry_history_and_lifecycle_details passes against the generator and fails against a copy whose HTML history call is removed, that copy being registered as the html-history-gate mutation case; verify_workable_items.py reports pdf-documents-current PASS with equal identifier sets for Issues and Fixed.
Evidence: scripts/workable_items.py(long_form_fields, history_lines); tests/test_workable_items.py(test_derived_documents_carry_history_and_lifecycle_details); scripts/verify_workable_items.py(html-history-gate mutation case); evidence/workable-items/results-2026-11-20T2036-before-pdf-history-fix.json; evidence/campaign-2026-11-20/containers/distribution.log

- 2026-11-20 Fixed (AI): one field source feeds Markdown, HTML and PDF; identifier sets now agree across formats and the history drop is a rejected mutant

items.title: [HRD-026] Validate interoperability on real readers, OPDS clients, and remote providers

items.description:
Phase 1 landed: configurable catalog/AI-memory pools, distinct aimemory migration lock, durable scan records across restart, batched page child loads (measured 3.6x), and an additive keyset cursor through HTTP and OPDS with needle-proofed tests. First 50k-work measurements recorded in docs/scalability-review.md and evidence/campaign-2026-11-20/scalability/. DEFECT-003 (transport-contaminated and nondeterministic scale assertions) found and fixed. Identity locks are now scoped per work, edition and source instead of one global key: 5.85x write throughput in one process (271.94 -> 1592.21 ops/s) and 1.53x to 4.07x across separate OS processes, while the no-lock needle silently loses 8 of 480 concurrently merged editions (evidence/campaign-2026-11-20/lock-scope/ and .../multiprocess/). DEFECT-004: the multi-process needle was blind until a database barrier aligned process starts, because the unsafe window is only the first write to an identity that does not exist yet; the runner now refuses a run where the unlocked variant verifies clean. Concurrent read envelope measured at 1/8/32/64 clients with zero errors: indexed browse and OPDS plateau near 1000 req/s (repo) and 900 (HTTP), limited by database CPU rather than the pool (pool=64 probe 942 vs 992 req/s, zero pool waits), while unanchored %text% search plateaus near 9 req/s at p99 12.0 s with pool starvation stacked on that wall. Release gate still unmet: no ratified SLO, no ingest-concurrent-with-reads test, and content delivery, KOSync/Redis and remote-source connectors remain unmeasured under load. Vector search measured and fixed: Search carried the id tiebreak inside the ORDER BY distance clause, an ordering no pgvector index can satisfy, so every search scanned and sorted every stored embedding while the HNSW index was still maintained on insert (DEFECT-005). Moved outside the subquery: 28.3 ms -> 1.86 ms p50 and 172.8 -> 2748 req/s at 32 clients, 50k rows x 384 dims, and the index path is now chosen without being forced. The harness refuses to be trusted on its own word: catalog-level schema comparison, per-connection session attestation, and a cardinality-independent plan control, with a nine-mutation gate at 9/9 (evidence/campaign-2026-11-20/vector/). New open question, not a defect: hnsw.ef_search (compile-time default 40) is not configurable anywhere in the product, and recall@10 against an exhaustive scan of the same fixture is 0.1025 at that width on 384-dim uniform vectors, 0.5475 at width 400.

Severity: Critical
Registry status: In progress
Reopens: 0
Affected scope: PostgreSQL writes and search, API pagination, job retention, and connection pools.
Reproduction: Measured and addressed: offset pagination (keyset cursor), per-work child-query fan-out (batched loads), catalog pool caps, and global write serialization, which is now one advisory lock per touched work/edition/source instead of one key for every writer (5.85x on disjoint concurrent merges in a single in-container run, at 89% of the unlocked ceiling; invariants carried by server/internal/catalog/lock_scope_test.go with paired needles and a key-class mutation gate).
